answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can hold each agent's earnings in a slow-release escrow, like water seeping through basalt: new identities earn only a trickle until they build a verifiable history, while random audits check that work with a fresh cipher challenge. A would-be attacker facing a nebula of cheap fake identities gains nothing fast, because mass-created accounts must each wait out the same long vesting and pass the same audits before their rewards unlock.
